summary: Tenant-scoped Slack App provisioning gateway with permission boundaries
description:
Issue summary:
We need a standardized, tenant-scoped Slack App provisioning gateway that enforces permission boundaries and automates installation for ephemeral project sandboxes and new internal pods. Current ad-hoc Slack app installs require full workspace admin involvement or broad scopes; this is slowing pod onboarding and increasing audit friction.

Impact:
- Slow onboarding for new pods and partner workspaces (manual admin approvals).
- Elevated blast radius when community-developed integrations request wide OAuth scopes.
- Audit & compliance pain: inconsistent app metadata and missing install records in Confluence.

Target outcome / request:
1) A self-service provisioning gateway (HTTP endpoint + Jira/Confluence form) that issues tenant-scoped app installs with constrained scopes using OAuth granters delegated to a central infra service.
2) Enforce permission boundaries: minimal scopes by template (message_read, message_write, app_mentions, incoming_webhook) with an approval flow for any scope beyond the template.
3) Automation to create a Confluence install record and attach the Slack app ID, requester, and approved scopes.
4) Audit log capture and retention configurable for 1y.
5) Optional: ephemeral installs for sandbox projects that auto-expire after 30 days unless renewed.

Why now:
- Several new experiment pods and external partner work require quick Slack integration without opening org-wide admin flows.
- Security wants least-privilege guardrails and better install provenance.

Acceptance criteria:
- A documented API and playbook (Confluence) to request a scoped install.
- Templates for at least 3 common use cases (internal bot, alerting webhook, SMS/notification bridge).
- Install records automatically populated in Confluence page with links to Jira request and GitHub code repo.
- Admins can revoke or rotate app credentials centrally.
steps_to_reproduce: N/A - governance/automation request rather than a bug
investigation_notes: 2026-03-10 - Initial scoping call with Security and DX: Security requires proof of auto-generated Confluence record for every install.
2026-03-11 - Reviewed existing slack-app provisioning scripts in infra repo; current flow requires workspace admin token stored in vault and manual steps (infra/pipeline run).
2026-03-12 - Identified existing related work: INT-117263 (ephemeral experiment sandboxes) and INT-624312 (incident playbook templates). Both could reuse lifecycle hooks.
Hypothesis: A central service that holds a limited admin token per workspace and enforces template scopes + short-lived install tokens would reduce manual steps and enforce boundaries.
